conviction_note: The event is confirmed on the issuer's calendar for 29 Sep and every CBG results RNS lands at 07:00. My fundamental read is a small beat on FY26 adjusted operating profit (about +4% against the £111m company-compiled consensus), and CET1 should print near Q3's 14.3% against a stale consensus of 13.8%. But this stock trades on motor finance, the dividend and the FY27 guide, not on AOP: 12 of its last 14 prints closed down, the H1 AOP beat fell 3.5%, and the Upper Tribunal timetable (hearing Dec 2026 or Feb 2027) means the dividend condition the board set ('further clarity') cannot yet be met. So p_up is 48 on an abs move of 6.5, which gives a signed -0.3. The findings sum to -0.3.

new_in_release.expect: FY26 AOP about £114-118m against the £111m consensus. That is a small beat, built from opex below £450m and bad debt near 0.8%. The company has already guided to both, so it is mostly inside guidance. Slightly positive for the number, near zero for the stock.

This is the first FY27 guide: the cost base after £60m of savings, NIM around 7%, loan growth of 5-10%, and possibly a Basel 3.1 quantification. Consensus FY27 AOP is £140m and CET1 12.3%. I cannot predict the direction, and the move lives here.

No FY26 final dividend, as all six consensus analysts assume. The risk is that the board ties reinstatement explicitly to the tribunal judgment (spring 2027 or later), which threatens the 14.5p FY27 consensus. That leans negative, with low confidence.

The year-end IAS 37 motor finance provision is the first audited one since the tribunal suspension and the 1 Sep Consumer Voice filings. I expect it to be held around £320m, with a small top-up risk. It leans negative.
CET1 at 31 July is probably about 14.2-14.4% (Q3 14.3%, plus Q4 profit, minus the AT1 coupon and RWA growth), against a 13.8% consensus mean. Mildly positive.

findings.finding: FY26 CET1 should print near 14.3% (Q3 was 14.3% after the £30m provision top-up, and Q4 profit roughly offsets the June AT1 coupon and about 1% loan growth). The company-compiled consensus mean is 13.8% (range 13.0-14.3%), so every contributor expects a flat or lower ratio and the mean is dragged by stale estimates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26: CET1 rose from 13.8% to 14.3% with AOP ahead of expectations, and the stock still fell 3.52% on the day (baseline history 2026-03-17). Capital beats have not been paid on this name while motor finance is open.

findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 14.3% is public, so most of this is already known. The unpriced part is only the headline comparison on the day ('CET1 14.x% vs consensus 13.8%'). If the market were anchored on 13.8%, the stock would trade near RBC's 470p rather than at 0.45x TNAV of 870p. That it does not suggests the market already reads capital at around Q3, which is why this finding is small.
findings.independence: The Q3 trading statement gives CET1 14.3% at 30 April 2026 after the provision (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/close-brothers-group--cbg/trading-statement/9578771). It is a different document but the same underlying number.

findings.finding: The board's stated condition for reinstating the dividend ('once there is further clarity on the financial impact') cannot be met at this print. The Upper Tribunal partially suspended the FCA scheme on 2 July, the hearing is set for 14-18 Dec 2026 or 16-26 Feb 2027 with judgment 'in the months following', and on 1 Sep Consumer Voice's filings alleged a Treasury steer to cap payouts, which widens the range upward. So the FY26 results, the first audited year-end provision since the suspension, are more likely to push the dividend timetable out and add caution to the £320m provision than to settle anything.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Motor finance and dividend news has driven every large move: -22.51% on 2024-02-15 (dividend suspended and provisions), -21.54% on 2025-03-18 (H1 provision), about -9% on the Viceroy report of 2026-03-16, -2.57% on the 2026-05-21 £30m top-up, and about -5% on the RBC downgrade of 2026-07-06.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: RBC told clients in July to expect the dividend to be delayed, all six consensus analysts have FY26 DPS at 0, the stock is down 11% over 60 days and shorts are edging up. What is not priced is FY27, where consensus still carries 14.5p DPS. A board statement tying reinstatement to a judgment that may not arrive before mid-2027 would cut that number, and the price does not look like it expects a lost FY27 dividend at 0.45x TNAV. I sized this small because it agrees with the building short and the run-down.
findings.independence: RBC, 6 Jul 2026, expects the dividend to be delayed and prices the scrapped-scheme tail at ~£200m (https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/close-brothers-shares-drop-5-following-rbc-downgrade-over-motor-finance-fears-4756739). CityAM, 1 Sep 2026, reports the Consumer Voice filings (https://www.cityam.com/treasury-sought-to-cap-motor-finance-payouts-court-filings-claim/).

outside_window.finding: Upper Tribunal hearing on the four challenges to the FCA motor finance redress scheme (Consumer Voice, VW FS, Mercedes-Benz FS, Crédit Agricole Auto Finance). The outcome decides whether CBG's £320m provision holds, or whether it faces RBC's ~£200m scrapped-scheme tail.

language_note: The domestic primary sources carried the bar: the company-compiled consensus PDF on the issuer's IR site (FY26 AOP £111m, CET1 13.8%, FY27 DPS 14.5p, and the note that one of six estimates predates Q3). No English wire preview I found quoted any of it.

lessons_applied: Dropped the FY26 AOP-beat finding (+0.3). It rests on opex 'below £450m' and bad debt near 0.8%, both already guided in the 21 May trading update, and reported_quarter findings went 4 of 14 on sign. The H1 AOP beat on this name was sold (-3.5%). The fundamental read stays in print_vs_bar_pct (+4).
Cut the CET1 finding from +0.5 to +0.3, because the Q3 14.3% is already public and only the stale consensus comparison is new.

Cut the dividend/provision finding from -1.0 to -0.6, because it agrees with a building short register and a -11% 60-day run-down, so it is largely priced ('positioning is the thing to beat, not to agree with').

Raised abs_move_pct from 5.0 to 6.5: this release carries the first FY27 guide and a dividend decision, which counts as a scheduled guidance event (median 9.0% against 2.3%), and hunters understated the move by a factor of about three. Q3 pre-released part of the year, so I did not go to 9.
